title: Water Cycle Basics
summary: This lesson explores the water cycle and how water moves above and below the Earth's surface. Students will learn the processes of evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection using visual descriptions.

sections.text: Scene: A diagram showing a glowing sun above the Earth's surface, with blue arrows illustrating water moving both above and below the ground. I wonder...?: How does water move around the Earth's surface? Answer: The water cycle describes how water moves above and below the Earth's surface.

Scene: Heat rays from the sun turn liquid water into vapor rising upward, which then cools high in the sky to form white clouds. I wonder...?: How do clouds form in the sky? Answer: Evaporation turns liquid water into vapor using heat from the sun, and condensation forms clouds when vapor cools high in the sky.

Scene: Clouds release water down toward the ground as rain or snow, which then gathers as runoff into rivers, lakes, and oceans. I wonder...?: How does water return to the Earth? Answer: Precipitation returns water as rain or snow, and collection gathers runoff into rivers, lakes, and oceans.

learning_objectives: Describe how water moves above and below the Earth's surface
Identify the roles of evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection in the water cycle
